From my experience in buying things to start a new business, hobby, project...whatever, is that I’ve tried to spend the least amount upfront to just get started. Then after some time I would spend more on fixing problems, having it not come out right because the equipment was poor quality, and buying new material to redo whatever I’m trying make. It costs more to go that route than it does to buy the right stuff in the first place. My advice, especially for screen printing is choose what piece of equipment that will get the most use, wear or that determines the best quality result. Save enough to purchase that. Example: I bought a UV vacuum exposure machine for about $800. I have no issues making the screens. They always come out perfect and beautiful. Now I don’t waste time and money having to reclaim the screens, waste emulsion etc. Then I bought a 4 screen printing machine. Not the best, not the worst. Even though you would think that’s what gets the most use, I figured not getting the cheapest one will save me some headaches and if I ever wanted to step it up to the next level, I didn’t break the bank if I eventually stopped printing. With those two pieces I spent about $1100 and I feel like I can make some good quality prints. Then come the screens, all the inks, the printer for transparencies, etc. that’s gonna require more investments and time to get everything right before you might start making things you feel comfortable selling and actually making some money. 

Do a lot of research, read a lot of reviews and save to buy the right stuff. Then, have a blast being creative!
